title: Argumentative Essay Rubric
description: For a single-author argumentative essay of roughly 500–900 words.

criteria.name: Claim & Thesis
criteria.description: A precise, arguable thesis in the introduction that previews the main reasons.

levels.label: Exemplary
levels.description: Precise, arguable thesis early on; previews the main lines of reasoning.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.description: Clear, arguable thesis; preview of reasons is partial.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Thesis is vague, overly broad, or appears late.

levels.label: Beginning
levels.description: No identifiable thesis, or the thesis is a statement of fact.

criteria.name: Evidence & Accuracy
criteria.description: Specific, relevant and accurate evidence supports every reason.

levels.label: Exemplary
levels.description: Specific, accurate evidence (statistics, examples, cases) for every reason.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.description: Evidence supports most reasons; minor vagueness.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: General, thin or partly irrelevant evidence; one factual error.

levels.label: Beginning
levels.description: Little or no evidence, or several factual errors.

criteria.name: Reasoning & Analysis
criteria.description: Explains how each piece of evidence proves the claim.

levels.label: Exemplary
levels.description: Explains how each piece of evidence proves the claim; logical and insightful.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.description: Analysis for most evidence, sometimes summary-like.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Evidence is mostly listed rather than explained.

levels.label: Beginning
levels.description: Claims asserted without support or explanation.

criteria.name: Counterclaim & Rebuttal
criteria.description: Fairly states a serious opposing view and rebuts it.

levels.label: Exemplary
levels.description: States a serious opposing view fairly and rebuts it convincingly.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.description: Acknowledges a counterclaim; brief rebuttal.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Straw-man counterclaim or missing rebuttal.

levels.label: Beginning
levels.description: No counterclaim.

criteria.name: Organization & Coherence
criteria.description: Every paragraph serves the thesis, in a logical order with clear transitions.

levels.label: Exemplary
levels.description: Every paragraph serves the thesis; logical order; clear topic sentences and transitions.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.description: Mostly focused and ordered; one weak transition.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: One paragraph is off-topic or out of place.

levels.label: Beginning
levels.description: Disorganized; frequent digressions.

criteria.name: Language & Conventions
criteria.description: Precise, formal style; essentially free of errors.

levels.label: Exemplary
levels.description: Precise, formal style; essentially error-free.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.description: A few minor errors that do not distract.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Repeated errors (agreement, homophones, articles) that distract.

levels.label: Beginning
levels.description: Errors frequently obscure meaning.

notes: Personal anecdotes that do not support the thesis count against Organization & Coherence.
A factual inaccuracy lowers Evidence & Accuracy even if the surrounding argument is strong.
Judge the overall pattern of errors under Language & Conventions; do not deduct twice for one error.
